title: [claude draft] Bell's first phone call (1876)
note: Claude draft, not Nandu's final script. Narration is exactly as drafted. Tags are Claude's own tagging, so the score tests the tagging, not the script. Historical facts are not yet checked against sources.
logline: Bell spills battery acid and his cry for help becomes the first phone call.
narration: March tenth, eighteen seventy-six. Boston. Alexander Graham Bell is in his workshop. Three days ago he got a patent for a talking wire. But nobody has heard it work. His helper, Thomas Watson, waits in the next room, holding the receiver. Bell leans over his machine. Then he knocks over a jar of battery acid. It spills on his clothes. He shouts into the device: "Mr. Watson, come here. I want to see you." In the next room, Watson hears a voice. A real voice, coming out of a wire. He runs to the door. The first phone call is not a speech. It is a cry for help. Within a few years, thousands of homes had a phone. And it all began with a spill.
